summary: Quiet park-side kerb on a flat mid-section, but it's open roadside on a 60 km/h road with no marked parking lane.
reasons: Flattest, clearest stretch faces sports oval, away from houses
No marked parking lane on a 60 km/h tertiary road
Start is cluttered with a crossing, islands and angled bays

criteria.room: The first ~20 m (chunk1, at the junction) is cluttered with a pedestrian crossing, painted traffic islands and angled parking bays serving the oval, so it isn't usable. From roughly 50-110 m along the kerb the road edge runs clear and straight beside open parkland with no driveways, giving around 40-50 m of genuinely clear kerb. There is no painted parking lane or shoulder anywhere, though - a van would sit on the live edge of a 2-lane, 60 km/h road.
criteria.frontage: Almost entirely sports parkland on the kerb's own side - a playing field and a cricket oval with a visible red pitch. Houses sit across the road, set back and screened by trees, with a denser row appearing near the eastern end close to a busier junction.
criteria.overlooked: Very few windows face the spot directly: the near side is open grass/oval, and the opposite-side houses are across a two-lane road, partly hidden by trees. Overlook is low along most of the usable stretch.
criteria.slope: Grade swings sharply along the kerb: a steep ~15% descent over the first ~50 m (4.81 m down to 2.1 m), a flat, near-0% section from about 50-110 m (2.1-2.3 m), then a steep ~15% climb over the final ~50 m up to 7.3 m. The flat middle section - which also has the clearest frontage - is the only comfortable place to park; either end is too steep to sleep on.
criteria.disturbance: Tertiary road, 60 km/h, lit, two lanes, feeding a visibly busier multi-lane road with turn lanes at the eastern end, so expect more traffic noise there. The western end sits at a junction with a pedestrian crossing and traffic islands, adding turning-traffic noise.
criteria.shade: Good tree cover along much of the route, especially near the western junction and over the parkland stretch - useful morning shade, with some risk of sap/leaf drop from overhanging canopy.
criteria.signs_vs_imagery: No cyan sign dots appear in either image set, consistent with the empty signs list. Esri (2025) and QLD (2022) agree closely on layout; the painted crossing, islands and angled parking bays near the start are visible in both and aren't captured by the sign screen.

cannot_judge: Street lighting brightness at the parkland section
Actual kerb height and any no-stopping/clearway restriction on this 60 km/h road beyond what signs screen found
Whether the road edge has a formal shoulder wide enough for a van versus just a painted line
